competitor_alerts: WIN — The /shabbat page is fixed and live. Last week it served the homepage title with a canonical pointing at the homepage and a body that read only 'Loading this week's Shabbat menu...'. It now returns the correct title ('Shabbat Box | Kosher Shabbat Meals Delivered in Dallas'), a self-referencing canonical, and fully crawlable content including this week's menu (Lemon Herb Grilled Chicken, Pesto Roasted Potatoes, Garlic Green Beans, Summer Kale Salad) and all three price tiers ($65 / $115 / $225). Expect indexing to take 1–3 weeks.

WIN — THR is now listed on dallaskosher.org, on BOTH the /restaurants page and the /new-page-1 catering page, with a 2026 kosher certificate PDF. That was last week's #3 recommendation and it is done. This is the highest-authority local citation in the niche.

PROBLEM WITH THAT WIN — the Dallas Kosher catering listing's 'Click for contact' button points to https://thehungryroostertx.com/page/catering, which does not exist (there is no /page route in the app; the real URL is /catering). Every prospect who clicks THR's link from the single most authoritative kosher directory in Dallas lands on a 404, and the backlink passes no equity to the catering page. Competitor listings on the same page (AKC, A Taste of the World, Simcha, Gourmet Palate) all link correctly and all include a phone number in the listing text — THR's listing has no phone number or address at all.

NEW COMPETITOR — Olive & Fig (2909 W 15th St, Plano) has appeared on the Dallas Kosher restaurant list as an upscale Mediterranean restaurant and bar, positioned on 'elevated' dining and events. That is the same 'elevated / creative catering' language THR uses in its own Dallas Kosher blurb, so it competes directly for simcha and event budgets.

NEW COMPETITOR — Shi-Ya Modern Asian Cuisine, a 100% kosher sushi concept from the Meat Point owners, opened at 7114 Campbell Road and was covered by the Dallas Observer in its June 2026 restaurant-openings roundup (https://www.dallasobserver.com/food-drink/new-dallas-restaurants-opened-june-2026-40693920/). That is exactly the kind of local press backlink THR still has zero of.

COMPETITOR MOMENTUM — JGourmet, which outranks THR for 'Jewish catering Dallas', has opened its new Kosher Dairy Kitchen and cafe at the JCC and now runs a dedicated domain (jgourmetdallas.com) alongside its jccdallas.org page. It is building a second ranking asset for the same keyword THR is stuck at ~#8 for.

STRUCTURAL — Yelp pages appeared in the results for five of the seven target keywords. THR does have a Yelp listing (yelp.com/biz/the-hungry-rooster-dallas, last updated June 2026), but it did not surface anywhere in the 'kosher Dallas site:yelp.com' top 10, which this week was Aderet, Meat Point, Milk and Honey, CCCP Market, Weinberger's, Cattleack, Tokyo Bar, Midtown Pizza, Deli News and Benny's Bagels. Simcha ranks with only 11 reviews, so the bar to displace them is low.

STRUCTURAL — Delivery keywords remain owned by aggregators. DoorDash, Uber Eats and Postmates take nearly all of page 1 for both 'kosher delivery Dallas' and 'kosher meal delivery Texas'. THR is named inside those aggregator pages but has no owned URL competing there.

recommendations.action: Add a defensive redirect in next.config.ts from /page/:slug* to /:slug* (permanent), so /page/catering resolves to /catering regardless of whether Dallas Kosher updates the link.

A 301 recovers the traffic and the link equity immediately and costs about three lines of config. It also catches any other stale /page/... links pointing at the site.

The sameAs URL is also wrong, which breaks the entity link to the Facebook page and wastes the strongest social signal available.

recommendations.action: Add aggregateRating and a Review array to the homepage Restaurant JSON-LD, populated from the reviews already stored in Supabase and rendered on /reviews.

Competitors ranking above THR — Simcha with 11 Yelp reviews — win on visible social proof. This converts review data THR already owns into gold stars on a result it already has.

summary: Two of last week's high-priority fixes landed: the /shabbat page now serves correct metadata and fully crawlable menu content, and The Hungry Rooster is finally listed on dallaskosher.org on both the restaurant and catering pages. The catch is that the new Dallas Kosher catering listing links to /page/catering, a URL that does not exist, so the best backlink in the niche currently dumps every visitor on a 404. Rankings are otherwise flat — still page 1 for 'kosher catering Dallas' (~#10) and 'Jewish catering Dallas' (~#8) only — but a bonus check found THR at roughly #3 for 'kosher Shabbat meal delivery Dallas order online', the first evidence that the long-tail Shabbat strategy is working.
